import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import norm, t, skewnorm

# 1. Configuration of the 6 strategies
strategies = [
    {
        "title": "Aggressive Own-Half 4th-Downs",
        "family": "student_t",
        "params": {"nu": 5.0, "mu": 0.45, "sigma": 0.25}
    },
    {
        "title": "Early-Down Heavy Passing",
        "family": "skew_normal",
        "params": {"xi": 0.18, "omega": 0.58, "alpha": 3.5}
    },
    {
        "title": "Early-Down Dime Personnel",
        "family": "normal",
        "params": {"mu": 0.35, "sigma": 0.3061}
    },
    {
        "title": "Early-Game 2-Point Attempt",
        "family": "student_t",
        "params": {"nu": 3.0, "mu": 0.15, "sigma": 0.40}
    },
    {
        "title": "Heavy-Personnel Up-Tempo (13-P)",
        "family": "skew_normal",
        "params": {"xi": -0.10, "omega": 0.65, "alpha": 2.0}
    },
    {
        "title": "Physical Jamming of Outlet Back",
        "family": "normal",
        "params": {"mu": 0.28, "sigma": 0.2194}
    }
]

# Initialize subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(14, 18))
axes = axes.flatten()

for i, strat in enumerate(strategies):
    ax = axes[i]
    fam = strat["family"]
    p = strat["params"]
    
    # Instantiate distributions and find key locations
    if fam == "normal":
        dist = norm(loc=p["mu"], scale=p["sigma"])
        mode = p["mu"]
    elif fam == "student_t":
        dist = t(df=p["nu"], loc=p["mu"], scale=p["sigma"])
        mode = p["mu"]
    elif fam == "skew_normal":
        dist = skewnorm(p["alpha"], loc=p["xi"], scale=p["omega"])
        # Locate mode numerically for the skew normal distribution
        x_dense = np.linspace(p["xi"] - 4 * p["omega"], p["xi"] + 4 * p["omega"], 50000)
        mode = x_dense[np.argmax(dist.pdf(x_dense))]
    
    # Calculate internal intervals using the exact percentiles (ppf)
    low_95 = dist.ppf(0.025)
    high_95 = dist.ppf(0.975)
    
    # Generate broad x values for plotting to capture tails gracefully
    x = np.linspace(low_95 - 1.5 * (high_95 - low_95), high_95 + 1.5 * (high_95 - low_95), 2000)
    y = dist.pdf(x)
    
    # Plot components
    ax.plot(x, y, color="#1a5f7a", linewidth=2.5, label="Prior PDF")
    
    # Shade the 95% interval
    x_shade = np.linspace(low_95, high_95, 1000)
    ax.fill_between(x_shade, dist.pdf(x_shade), color="#57c5b6", alpha=0.35, label="95% Credible Interval")
    
    # Annotate markers
    ax.axvline(mode, color="#ef5b0c", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.8, label=f"Mode (Most Plausible): {mode:.3f}")
    ax.axvline(low_95, color="#002b5b", linestyle=":", linewidth=1.5)
    ax.axvline(high_95, color="#002b5b", linestyle=":", linewidth=1.5)
    
    # Titles, labels and styling
    ax.set_title(f"{strat['title']}\nFamily: {fam} {list(p.items())}", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", pad=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("Change in own scoring margin (points)", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Probability Density", fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8.5)
    ax.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)
    
    # Print analytical data to standard out
    print(f"Strategy: {strat['title']}")
    print(f"  Family: {fam}")
    print(f"  Parameters: {p}")
    print(f"  Computed 95% Interval: [{low_95:.4f}, {high_95:.4f}]")
    print(f"  Computed Mode: {mode:.4f}\n")

plt.suptitle("Prior Probability Distributions of Expected Scoring Margin Effects", fontsize=15, fontweight="bold", y=0.99)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

prior.consistency_check: The most plausible value of 0.45 is centered inside the symmetric interval [-0.19, 1.09]. The Student-t distribution supports negative values, representing the risk of backfiring.

distribution_family.justification: The potential outcomes of aggressive own-half 4th-down decisions have heavy tails; a failure can occasionally lead to a disastrous quick touchdown for the opponent, while success significantly sustains scoring drives.
distribution_family.name: student_t

parameters.conversion_note: With nu = 5.0, the t-critical value at 95% confidence is 2.571. Sigma is derived as (1.09 - (-0.19)) / (2 * 2.571) = 1.28 / 5.142 = 0.25.

strategies.rationale: Public expected-points (EP) and win-probability (WP) models demonstrate that the reward of maintaining possession and continuing a drive far outweighs the risk of giving the opponent a short field on this thin margin. Traditional coaching overvalues the safety of a punt, which frequently net-yields only 35-40 yards of field position while sacrificing a highly valuable possession.
strategies.recommendation: Attempt conversions on fourth down and 2 or less when inside our own 30 to 39-yard line, rather than automatically punting. This is especially critical in the first three quarters of the game.
strategies.title: Aggressive Own-Half 4th-Downs

prior.consistency_check: The most plausible value of 0.54 lies comfortably within the skewed 95% interval of [0.21, 1.62]. The distribution supports negative values, although the mass is concentrated on the positive side.

distribution_family.justification: Explosive pass plays have an infinite upside tail on early downs, whereas the downside of an incomplete pass or sack is bounded and well-understood, yielding a right-skewed prior distribution.
distribution_family.name: skew_normal

parameters.conversion_note: Fitted numerically. With location xi = 0.18, scale omega = 0.58, and shape alpha = 3.5 (indicating a strong right skew), the distribution's mode is approximately 0.54, and the 95% interval spans from 0.21 to 1.62.

strategies.rationale: Pass plays on early downs yield a substantially higher EPA (Expected Points Added) on average than run plays. Passing from heavy personnel groups forces the defense into run-defense shells and heavier linebackers, creating massive windows for explosive pass-action plays downfield.
strategies.recommendation: Pass the ball on at least 65% of first-and-10 plays when executing from run-heavy personnel packages (12 or 21 personnel). This creates highly favorable matchups against base defensive fronts.
strategies.title: Early-Down Heavy Passing

prior.consistency_check: The most plausible value of 0.35 is exactly at the midpoint of the symmetric interval [-0.25, 0.95]. The distribution supports both positive and negative values.

distribution_family.justification: The outcome is modeled symmetrically with moderate tails, as the variance of early-down run defense versus pass protection outcomes is well-bounded and predictable.
distribution_family.name: normal

parameters.conversion_note: Using standard normal properties: sigma = (high - low) / 3.92 = (0.95 - (-0.25)) / 3.92 = 1.20 / 3.92 = 0.3061.

strategies.rationale: Analytics models consistently show that stopping explosive pass plays is the single most critical driver of defensive success. Giving up a marginal success rate on early-down runs is a highly favorable trade-off compared to risking coverage busts in base personnel against modern spread passing concepts.
strategies.recommendation: Deploy a light-box, dime personnel package (six defensive backs) on first-and-10 situations to guard against the deep pass, inviting the opponent to run.
strategies.title: Early-Down Dime Personnel

prior.consistency_check: The most plausible value of 0.15 is centered in the symmetric interval [-1.12, 1.42]. The support covers signed real values.

distribution_family.justification: This choice introduces highly volatile psychological factors. The heavy tails reflect a non-trivial chance of a massive positive behavioral effect, balanced against a negative swing if we miss and spiral defensively.
distribution_family.name: student_t

parameters.conversion_note: With nu = 3.0, the t-critical value is 3.182. Sigma is calculated as (1.42 - (-1.12)) / (2 * 3.182) = 2.54 / 6.364 = 0.40.

strategies.rationale: Public analytics is silent or mixed on this because models do not track qualitative factors. My intuition is that establishing an aggressive posture early physically forces the opposing coach to abandon their game plan, inducing panic and forcing them to play 'catch up' with their own subsequent decision-making.
strategies.recommendation: Attempt a two-point conversion on our very first touchdown of the game, regardless of the score or time remaining, to break the opponent's defensive script.
strategies.title: Early-Game 2-Point Attempt

prior.consistency_check: The most plausible value of 0.25 is inside the interval [-0.28, 1.25], and the distribution supports negative values.

distribution_family.justification: There is a massive positive ceiling if the opposing defense gets stuck and physically gasps, but a slight negative downside if we go three-and-out quickly, exhausting our own defense.
distribution_family.name: skew_normal

parameters.conversion_note: Fitted numerically. With location xi = -0.10, scale omega = 0.65, and shape alpha = 2.0 (moderate right skew), the distribution's mode is approximately 0.25, and the 95% interval is approximately [-0.28, 1.25].

strategies.rationale: Analytics models generally evaluate tempo and personnel in isolation. Coaching intuition suggests that running up-tempo with heavy packages prevents defensive coordinators from substituting their pass-defense personnel, resulting in severe physical fatigue for interior defensive linemen and mismatch opportunities.
strategies.recommendation: Utilize a rapid, no-huddle up-tempo offense when operating out of heavy 13-personnel (1 RB, 3 TE, 1 WR) to freeze defensive packages.
strategies.title: Heavy-Personnel Up-Tempo (13-P)

prior.consistency_check: The most plausible value of 0.28 is centered within the symmetric interval [-0.15, 0.71]. The distribution natively covers signed real values.

distribution_family.justification: The performance distribution is expected to be highly consistent and stable. Symmetrical normal tails adequately represent the marginal improvements in coverage timing.
distribution_family.name: normal

parameters.conversion_note: Using standard normal properties: sigma = (high - low) / 3.92 = (0.71 - (-0.15)) / 3.92 = 0.86 / 3.92 = 0.2194.

strategies.rationale: Public tracking metrics classify coverage types broadly but fail to isolate the micro-impact of breaking check-down timing. Coaching intuition dictates that disrupting the safety valve immediately destroys the rhythm of West Coast offenses, forcing elite quarterbacks into lower-probability downfield windows.
strategies.recommendation: Assign a athletic, physical defender (safety or hybrid linebacker) to physically check and jam the opponent's primary receiving running back at the line of scrimmage on every play.
strategies.title: Physical Jamming of Outlet Back
